paragraphs: CoProcure runs Pavilion, which gives public agency buyers cooperative contracts and quick quotes from vendors that meet their compliance needs. It is free for public agencies, paid for by suppliers who buy premium features to grow their public sector business.

Buyers search a database of cooperatives, state contracts and their own agency's contracts in one place. The company puts that at 300,000 vendors on more than 100,000 contracts from cooperatives, states and local agencies. An agency's compliance requirements are embedded in every search, which is meant to prevent costly mistakes. A smart intake tool routes every request to the best purchasing method based on the need and the agency's policies. A browser extension shows, on any vendor's website, whether that vendor is on a contract the agency can use.

The site says Pavilion connects vendors with buyers from more than 3,500 public agencies who are ready to purchase. On the vendor side, leads come from buyers who are ready to purchase before an RFP gets started. The company states there is no federal coverage, because Pavilion is built for local and education agencies. The founder says the company began from how hard it is to balance compliance requirements with departments that just want to get their work done.
